summary: EarthSong turns NASA Earth observation data into a synchronized map and soundscape. Users explore fire-related thermal detections over Angola and Africa using NASA FIRMS data and satellite imagery from NASA GIBS. Each detection becomes a sound event, so users can see and hear the same pattern, in the same place and time period. EarthSong makes Earth science accessible to people who cannot easily read charts or maps.
details:
EarthSong is a web application that combines visualization and sonification of NASA Earth observation data. The challenge we address is that Earth science is usually presented through visualizations alone, which limits who can engage with it. EarthSong adds a sound layer that represents the same data.

The application uses NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) data, which records thermal activity detected by MODIS and VIIRS instruments, and NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services) for satellite imagery. The user selects a region, starting with Angola and then the rest of Africa, and a time period. The map and the sound engine use the same data and the same time range. When the user moves the timeline, both the image and the sound change together.

Each detection is mapped to sound: the number of detections sets the number of sound events, fire radiative power (where available) sets intensity, geographic position sets the stereo placement, and temporal sequence sets rhythm. To avoid overwhelming noise, detections are grouped by region and time interval, and every sound keeps a link to its original record.

Scientific accuracy is a priority. A thermal detection from satellite is not the same as a confirmed fire, so EarthSong presents the data as thermal activity detections and shows confidence indicators when available. The current stage is a design and architecture proposal. Real FIRMS data loading and the sound engine are the next development steps.
